source: Foster and Wilson (2006) Reverse replay of behavioural sequences in hippocampal place cells during the awake state
finding: First report that awake rats replay recent paths in reversed order right after the run. The authors link this to evaluating event sequences as in reinforcement learning.
numbers: Abstract page only read this session. Full-text numbers not verified here.
quote: recent episodes of spatial experience are replayed in a temporally reversed order
limits: Abstract only. Rat CA1, linear track. Numbers (event counts, time compression) not captured.
agent_relevance: Reverse replay is the hippocampal analogue of backing up credit from outcome to earlier steps. For an agent: after a result, walk the chain backwards from the outcome to assign credit (supports G2: revise from real output).

source: Diba and Buzsaki (2007) Forward and reverse hippocampal place-cell sequences during ripples
finding: On an elevated linear track, ripple-time sequences ran in reverse at the end of a run and in forward order before the run. So forward pre-run sequences were already seen in 2007, on known tracks.
numbers: 3 rats, 1,256 neurons total; only 267 fired >=5 Hz in both directions. 95% of significant forward events came before the run; 85% of significant reverse events came after the run.
quote: recurred in reverse order at the end of a run, but in forward order in anticipation of the run
limits: Familiar track, templates built from the same session's run, so this is anticipation of a known route, not preplay of a novel place.
agent_relevance: Two directions, two jobs: forward sequences before action look like planning or retrieval, reverse sequences after outcome look like credit assignment.

source: Davidson, Kloosterman, Wilson (2009) Hippocampal replay of extended experience
finding: On a 10.3 m track, replay covered long runs, in both directions, by chaining several ripple events. It ran at a steady virtual speed near 8 m/s.
numbers: 4 rats; 47, 34, 23, 32 units. Decoder median error 7, 9, 8, 8 cm. Candidate events 0.32 to 0.40 per second while stopped; 19% were long (>250 ms); event durations 40 to 1018 ms.
limits: Rats were not pre-trained, behaviour varied. Single lab, small n.
agent_relevance: Replay is built from short chunks chained together. A plan longer than one chunk needs chaining, like a multi-step plan in short context windows.

source: Karlsson and Frank (2009) Awake replay of remote experiences in the hippocampus
finding: Awake rats replayed a place sequence from another room, not the one they stood in. Remote replay was as common as local replay.
numbers: 3 rats. 288 of 612 candidate events (47%) in first exposure to E1 were significant replays of E1 (chance 5%). In the rest box 256 of 580 (44.1%) replayed E1. During long quiescence 373 of 1046 (35.7%) did; for >60 s immobility 106 of 310 (34.2%).
limits: Replay of earlier experience got less likely after long stillness, so retrieval strength depends on recent activity.
agent_relevance: Retrieval of a non-present context is the norm, not an error. A planner may need to pull in a different problem's solution on demand.

source: Dragoi and Tonegawa (2011) Preplay of future place cell sequences by hippocampal cellular assemblies
finding: Mice recorded in CA1 during rest on a familiar track. Place-cell firing order during rest matched the order on a novel arm they had not yet entered. The authors call this preplay. It was not just replay of the familiar track.
numbers: 3 mice. 14.2% of spiking events (>=4 novel-arm cells) were significant preplay (chance 3.2%; P<1e-32, binomial). 16.2% of familiar-track events were significant replay. 81.1% of preplay events were at the junction end. Pure replay vs pure preplay events: 171 vs 54, ratio about 3.1. 79.9% of events matched neither template.
quote: temporal sequences of firing of place cells expressed during a novel spatial experience occurred on a significant number of occasions during the resting or sleeping period preceding the experience
limits: Shuffle was 200 template shuffles, threshold 97.5th percentile. Only 3 mice for the contiguous design. The novel arm was joined to a familiar track, so it may be seen as an extension.
agent_relevance: The brain seems to hold a repertoire of ready sequences and bind one to a new case. An agent could keep a library of generic plan skeletons and select, not invent. Needs testing.

source: Dragoi and Tonegawa (2011) Preplay of future place cell sequences by hippocampal cellular assemblies (decoding and controls)
finding: Bayesian decoding of rest-time spikes showed time-compressed virtual trajectories inside the unvisited novel arm. Preplay events were better matched to the novel template than the familiar one.
numbers: Of decoded trajectories in Fam-Rest: 16.36% inside the novel arm (trajectory preplay), 64.15% replay of familiar track, 19.49% spanning both. Mean absolute rank correlation 0.75 (novel template) vs 0.59 (familiar), P<1e-4. 72% (n=54) of the 75 preplay events had no significant correlation with the familiar template; another 16% (n=12) fit the novel arm better (0.92 vs 0.67). Decoded trajectories were time-compressed (about 5 m/s virtual speed in the example). Silent cells perfectly matching the template: 16 of 24 triplets (0.67) vs chance 0.33.
limits: Percentages of decoded trajectories depend on line-fitting criteria. In 79.8% of trajectory-preplay cases shuffles gave significantly worse or no containment in the novel arm.
agent_relevance: The control logic (does the event match the new template more than the old one) is a model for testing whether an agent's plan is new or a copy of an old plan.

source: Dragoi and Tonegawa (2011) Preplay of future place cell sequences by hippocampal cellular assemblies (de novo experiment)
finding: Preplay also appeared in mice with no linear-track experience. Rest in a sleep box before a first novel track already held sequences matching that track.
numbers: 16.1% of spiking events in pre-run rest/sleep correlated with first-run place sequences, in all 4 mice. Median 6 place cells per preplay event. De novo place field stability r=0.42 vs 0.62 on the contiguous arm (P<0.016).
limits: Place fields on novel track were less stable than contiguous arm. Mouse CA1 only.
agent_relevance: Evidence that structure can exist before any task-specific experience, a link to priors in a pretrained model.

source: Dragoi and Tonegawa (2013) Distinct preplay of multiple novel spatial experiences in the rat
finding: Rats given three novel linear tracks showed preplay of each track, with high specificity. The authors estimate the network could preplay at least 15 tracks.
numbers: 3 naive rats, 1.5 m tracks. 9.8% of events were significant preplay. Preplay sequences covered 82.6% of track length on average (n=1,388; P<1e-200). 85.3% unidirectional. 4% of events decoded to novel-track trajectories (42.2% of track length). Track-specific preplay 6.65 to 6.8% per track; >90% specificity; 1.5% of events correlated with more than one track; 93.7% of cells active on >1 track; 78% of events matched none.
limits: Same lab as the original. The 15-tracks number is an extrapolation. Silva et al. 2015 failed to find preplay with other methods.
agent_relevance: If preplay is real, one network holds many candidate plans at once. This suggests generating several distinct plan candidates in parallel, each bound to a different case.

source: Dragoi and Tonegawa (2014) Selection of preconfigured cell assemblies for representation of novel spatial experiences
finding: Theory paper. A novel place-cell sequence is a selection from a repertoire of existing temporal sequences, not built from nothing. This is set against the blank-slate view (Locke) and the form view (Plato, Kant).
numbers: No new data. Summarises preplay of novel tracks and the capacity estimate.
limits: Position paper by the authors of the finding. Not independent.
agent_relevance: Names the design question: do new problems create new structure, or select from prior structure. For a scaffold, prior structure is the model's own pretraining.

source: Pfeiffer and Foster (2013) Hippocampal place-cell sequences depict future paths to remembered goals
finding: Rats in a 2 m x 2 m open arena with 36 reward wells and a goal that moved each day. Before moving, away-from-goal hippocampal sharp-wave events decoded trajectories that headed to the remembered goal and matched the path taken next.
numbers: 4 rats, 40 tetrodes, up to 250 neurons at once (CA1). 144 to 373 trajectory events per session (25.3% to 43.9% of candidates), mean duration 103.6 ms, path length 40.0 to 199.1 cm. 0 of 2,028 events had P>0.02 under shuffle. Away-events over-represented HOME: Grubbs outlier P D1 2.3e-2, D2 1.1e-2; end-at-HOME D1 6.9e-4, D2 6.0e-4. Future path vs past path angular displacement P=8.6e-31. Away vs home events to future path P=7.25e-16.
quote: the hippocampus generates brief sequences encoding spatial trajectories strongly biased to progress from the subject's current location to a known goal location
limits: Correlation with behaviour, no causal disruption in this paper. Open arena, 4 rats. Foraging phase less predictable.
agent_relevance: Strongest hippocampal evidence of planning: a candidate route is generated before acting, toward a goal. Fits: propose a plan, then act, then check against the real result.

source: Pfeiffer and Foster (2013) Hippocampal place-cell sequences depict future paths to remembered goals (novelty and flexibility)
finding: Events were flexible. HOME representation dropped before trips not going home. During the first 19 trials of a day, when start-goal pairs were new, events still matched the future path.
numbers: Away-events matched future path whether it ended at HOME or elsewhere (P 4.96e-22 and 1.12e-13). HOME representation lower before non-HOME trips (P=9.6e-3). Prior RANDOM well not over-represented; HOME vs previous RANDOM P 4.4e-16 (D1), 3.1e-20 (D2). First 19 trials: P=2.37e-10.
limits: Initiation bias: events start at the animal's current location, so only away-events test the goal effect.
agent_relevance: The planner composes a new route from known places, not a stored whole route. This is recombination, a core need for LLM plans over known tools.

source: Silva, Feng and Foster (2015) Trajectory events across hippocampal place cells require previous experience
finding: Failed to replicate preplay. With hundreds of units in rats on three novel tracks, pre-experience events were not correlated with later place order. Post-experience events were trajectory-like. NMDA-receptor block during experience prevented formation of trajectory events.
numbers: 4 rats, about 61 place cells per epoch on average. 9,803 Sleep-1 candidate events: median absolute correlation 0.174 actual vs 0.172 shuffle (p=0.08); with best-template choice 0.245 vs 0.258 (p=1). Levene p=0.44 and 0.77. L-ratio: 435 of 442 units (98%) well clustered. 86% of events at top or bottom fifth of track.
quote: they were not temporally correlated with subsequent experience
limits: Linear track, rats, versus mice in the original. Authors suggest the original bimodal-vs-unimodal histogram may reflect a shuffle mismatch. Preplay defenders reply that detection method matters.
agent_relevance: Direct contest on whether structure pre-exists. For us: do not assume a pre-built plan helps; require a held-out check (G3).

source: Silva, Feng and Foster (2015) Trajectory events across hippocampal place cells require previous experience (what experience changes)
finding: Post-experience events were better correlated, less jumpy, more sharply defined and more linear than pre-experience events. The authors call them trajectory events. The NMDA antagonist D-CPPene blocked their formation but not their retrieval.
numbers: Authors report the sleep-1 vs run-1 contrasts held across multiple measures. Drug-effect p-values are given per run in the paper; exact values not extracted here.
limits: Drug-effect numbers not fully extracted here; see paper for per-run statistics.
agent_relevance: Learning from experience is what makes sequences coherent. For an agent, in-context experience (real outputs) is what tightens a plan.

source: Olafsdottir, Barry, Saleem, Hassabis, Spiers (2015) Hippocampal place cells construct reward related sequences through unexplored space
finding: Preplay is goal-biased. Rats saw food placed in one of two unreachable T-maze arms. During rest after goal-cueing, place sequences for the cued arm were preplayed more than for the uncued arm.
numbers: 4 rats, 212 place cells. Cued arm: 7.37% preplay events (p<0.001, binomial vs chance). Uncued arm: 4.41% (p=0.33). Cued vs uncued p<0.001; AUC test cued vs uncued p=0.0044. RUN2 arm bias 0.96. Cued preplay equal in both directions (7.34% vs 7.40%). Cued template in REST1 not significant by AUC (p=0.14).
quote: viewing the delivery of food to an unvisited portion of an environment leads to off-line pre-activation of place cells sequences
limits: One animal had only 9 cued events. Different design from Dragoi (view but not enter). Positive for preplay, but only for rewarded space.
agent_relevance: Preplay seems tied to motivational relevance. Spend rollout budget on goal-relevant branches, not uniformly.

source: Grosmark and Buzsaki (2016) Diversity in neural firing dynamics supports both rigid and learned hippocampal sequences
finding: Reconciles both camps. Sequences in a novel environment mix a rigid, fast-firing subset (little change across sleep-experience-sleep) with a plastic, slow-firing subset that gains place specificity and ripple association.
numbers: 4 rats, 491 place cells, 8 novel sessions. 216 neurons strongly contributed to PRE or POST sequences; 73% of PRE contributors also contributed to POST (rigid). Rigid vs plastic split at median change in contribution.
quote: sequences of place-cell firing in a novel environment are formed from a combination of the contributions of a rigid, predominantly fast-firing subset
limits: Rat CA1, one lab, mixed analysis choices. Rigid cells have low spatial specificity.
agent_relevance: Two-part design: a fixed scaffold that is cheap to run plus a plastic part that learns. Matches fixed program plus model slots.

source: Ambrose, Pfeiffer, Foster (2016) Reverse replay of hippocampal place cells is uniquely modulated by changing reward
finding: Reverse replay rate rose when reward increased and fell when it decreased. Forward replay rate did not change. So direction has different jobs.
numbers: Poisson GLM on event rates. Reverse replay rate was greater than forward at the increased-reward site in epoch 2 (z about 4) and at the decreased-reward site in epoch 3 (z about 3). Exact digits truncated in extraction. SWR rate and replay rate both tracked reward increase.
limits: Exact z values not captured. Linear track, rats.
agent_relevance: Credit assignment (reverse) scales with surprise in reward; retrieval for choice (forward) does not. An agent should spend backward review on surprising outcomes (supports G1: act on signals).

source: Foster (2017) Replay Comes of Age
finding: Review by the author of the 2006 and 2013 papers. After about 20 years, many results force revision of original replay interpretations, with a focus on phenomenology.
numbers: Abstract page only read. No numbers captured.
limits: Abstract only. Not read in full.
agent_relevance: Pointer for later full-text reading in angle B or C.

source: Breffle, Germaine, Shin, Jadhav, Miller (2024) Intrinsic dynamics of randomly clustered networks generate place fields and preplay of novel environments
finding: Spiking network model with random clustered connectivity produces preplay of novel environments with no pre-set spatial map. Preplay is best in small-world regimes, high clustering with short path lengths.
numbers: Network of 15 clusters, mean cluster participation 1.25 (fiducial). Detected events: at least 50 ms and at least 5 cells. Decoding statistics follow Farooq et al. 2019 (weighted correlation, maximum jump distance). Model validated on rat W-track data (Shin et al. 2019).
quote: clustered recurrent connectivity can generate spontaneous preplay and immediate replay of novel environments
limits: Model, not an LLM. Shows a generic random network can produce preplay-like sequences, which weakens the claim that preplay proves pre-built maps.
agent_relevance: A random but structured prior can produce useful candidate sequences. Diversity from generic internal dynamics, then binding to the task.

source: Breffle et al. (2024) model: statistics and null tests
finding: Preplay in the model is graded by a two-criterion bootstrap (minimum weighted correlation and maximum jump). Permuting cell identity removes the correlation shift, as a control.
numbers: Permuted-network median preplay correlation shift centred on zero (t-test 95% CI includes 0). Cluster-bias order test compared with random cluster sampling in three-cluster events.
limits: The result depends on the thresholds chosen. Many events fail both criteria.
agent_relevance: A reminder: significance depends on shuffle and threshold choices. For agent checks, use fixed pre-registered null tests.

source: Farooq, Zhou, Sibille, Dragoi (2025) Generative emergence of non-local representations in the hippocampus
finding: Rats on a novel detour formed compressed theta sequences within 1 to 2 laps by reusing sequence motifs seen in pre-detour sleep. Pre-existing and detour representations flickered in different theta phases.
numbers: Abstract and front matter read. Quantities: 1 to 2 laps; adult male rats.
limits: Only the abstract-level text was extracted this session. Dragoi lab, pro-preplay. Author list partly inferred from front matter; check.
agent_relevance: Rapid reuse of old motifs for a new case, with alternate plans kept apart by phase. Suggests holding separate parallel plan candidates apart, not blended.

source: Dragoi and Tonegawa (2011), template and event definitions
finding: Definition of the test. A spiking event has >=4 cells, spikes less than 50 ms apart, flanked by 50 ms of silence. Spearman rank correlation to a template of place-peak order; significant if above the 97.5th percentile of 200 shuffles.
numbers: In 91% of preplay cases events correlated with the novel template in one direction only. Distribution of correlations shifted from shuffle (P<1e-32). Place field stability across sessions: median r 0.66 familiar track vs 0.23 shuffled (P<1e-4); novel arm 0.62 vs 0.21 (P<1e-3).
limits: Rank-order methods vary between labs (50 ms silence vs 100 ms; 4 vs 6 cells). Differences feed the replication dispute.
agent_relevance: Parameter choices in the detection test drive findings. For agent evaluation, fix and log the check rules before running.

source: Dragoi and Tonegawa (2013), event definition and cell overlap
finding: Second study used stricter events (>=6 cells, >100 ms silence, first spike only, 500 shuffles) and still found preplay.
numbers: Preplay threshold 97.5th percentile of 500 surrogate orderings. Similar results when all spikes were used. 93.7% of cells active on more than one track yet preplay specificity >90%.
limits: Same lab, same logic. Silva et al. (2015) reply that their different measures see no preplay.
agent_relevance: Robust to analysis choice inside one lab does not equal independent replication (G4: same source is not independent).

source: Silva, Feng and Foster (2015) Trajectory events across hippocampal place cells require previous experience (discussion)
finding: If preplay sequences dominated, replay could not serve as a sign of learning. Authors argue place cells start with place fields and learn the links between places, so replay reflects learned contingencies, not stored routes.
numbers: Notes the hippocampus can generate sequences in an order never experienced, and sequences to novel goals (citing Pfeiffer and Foster 2013), once the logic of the place graph is sampled.
limits: Interpretive. Authors favour learning over preconfiguration.
agent_relevance: Supports the view that planning is search over a learned graph of contingencies, not retrieval of full old plans.

source: Pfeiffer and Foster (2013), discussion of mechanism
finding: Authors argue simple route-encoding by direct experience cannot explain trial-by-trial goal switching or events for new start-goal pairs. They propose events link places to value or action that local theta look-ahead later uses.
numbers: Rats showed no bias to face the goal during away-events; away-events matched future path better than current heading.
limits: Speculation about mechanism; open whether events compute optimal paths around barriers.
agent_relevance: Two-stage idea for an agent: an offline plan sketch, then online local look-ahead, with the sketch biasing the local step.

source: Olafsdottir et al. (2015), controls
finding: Cued-arm preplay was not explained by cell counts, sorting quality or place-field stability. Arm interest during goal cue predicted each animal's preplay amount.
numbers: Template lengths 15 to 53 cells per arm. Cued arm stability r=0.54 vs uncued 0.49 (p=0.15). Neighbouring-field cluster separation p=0.45 (KS). Field location on arm p=0.22. Dwell-time cue bias 0.10 before vs 0.33 during goal cue.
limits: Tiny sample, 4 rats. Events defined as <=300 ms with >=15% of cells active, a looser rule than Dragoi 2011.
agent_relevance: Interest or salience steers which candidate gets rehearsed. Use goal-relevance to rank which branches to simulate.

source: Davidson et al. (2009), replay speed and chaining
finding: Authors argue earlier results on 1 to 2 m tracks fit a single ripple read-out, but long tracks need chains of subsequences. Replay stayed coherent across trains of ripple events.
numbers: Standard ripple is 50 to 120 ms; 10.3 m at about 8 m/s virtual speed implies over 1 s of total replay.
limits: Decoder uses unit ensembles, not just well-isolated single cells. Qualitatively same with well-isolated units.
agent_relevance: Long plans are chains of short coherent segments. A scaffold should chunk plans into short segments, check each, then join.

source: Foster and Wilson (2006), role in later disputes
finding: Reverse replay is the origin point for later reward-learning readings (Ambrose 2016) and for the idea that replay evaluates sequences.
numbers: See Ambrose 2016: reverse but not forward replay rate tracked reward changes.
limits: Link is an interpretation from the abstract plus a later paper.
agent_relevance: Reverse review after outcomes is a natural operator for the schema (check from the failing output backwards).
